I saw that I could put an end to your outrages by pronouncing a single word in my mind. I pronounced it. The word was ‘No.’" (Atlas Shrugged)
text_post: That reminds me of the “free love” hippies of the 1970s. Well, they found out that getting an abortion and getting medical treatment for STDs costs money. As they got older, many of them decided to shave, shower, finish their college degrees, and become corporate servants. I hate the idea of taxing a person’s land (other than the initial tax of the purchase price). If you buy something, it’s yours—in my world. You should also be able to give it to your family/friends without tax penalties. Here in the USA, we can’t really own land. We lease it from the government. Besides that, the natural forces of the world can disrupt the value of that “leased” land. I see the world as one big casino. You “roll the dice” every time you get out of bed and deal with people. “The house” lets you win a little after you or others lose a lot. Make safe bets, take some risks, or don’t play at all.
